title: Netlify Blocked My Site — Now It Deploys Itself | vitalii.no
description:
On 2026-09-26 Netlify exhausted the function-invocation quota on my entire hosting account and blocked it outright — largely from search-engine crawlers hammering the /news and /blog pages that had just been switched to server-side rendering for SEO. vitalii.no was left with no working host at all.

I replaced the managed host with infrastructure I run myself. A GitHub Actions workflow builds the Next.js app as a standalone server and uploads it as an artifact on every push. A deploy script on my own VPS pulls the newest build, unpacks it, flips a release symlink, and restarts the site service — checking its health up to 40 times before committing to the new release, and rolling back to the previous one automatically if it never comes up healthy. A timer runs this check every 2 minutes, with the existing Cloudflare tunnel and cache rule still sitting in front of the site.

vitalii.no now runs entirely off infrastructure I control, redeploying automatically within 2 minutes of every push, and a broken release rolls itself back instead of taking the whole site down the way the Netlify block did.
